name: layernorm
summary: LayerNorm over last dim for 2D row-major contiguous tensors. Fwd outputs (Y, Mean[M], Rstd[M]). Optional affine (Gamma/Beta). Bwd supports noaff (dX) and affine (dX + dGamma[f32,N] + dBeta[f32,N]). eps via AttrBlob schema 'LNEP' or schema_id==0 default.
contract: - Normalization axis: last dim N (per-row stats over N)
- noaff  inputs(1):  X                         outputs(3): Y, Mean[f32,M], Rstd[f32,M]
- affine inputs(3):  X, Gamma, Beta            outputs(3): Y, Mean[f32,M], Rstd[f32,M]
- noaff  inputs(4):  X, dY, Mean, Rstd         outputs(1): dX
- affine inputs(5):  X, dY, Gamma, Mean, Rstd  outputs(3): dX, dGamma[f32,N], dBeta[f32,N]
- f32 path: X,Y,dY,dX are f32; Gamma/Beta f32 when present; Mean/Rstd f32; dGamma/dBeta f32
- f16 path: X,Y,dY,dX are f16; Gamma/Beta f16 when present; Mean/Rstd f32; dGamma/dBeta f32
- Mean and Rstd are 1D contiguous length M
- Gamma/Beta (if present) are 1D contiguous length N
- dGamma/dBeta (if present) are 1D contiguous length N
- No explicit aliasing guarantee; treat as out-of-place unless runtime ensures safety.
- if affine: y = xhat * gamma + beta else y = xhat
- dy_hat = dy * gamma (or dy if no gamma)
- dX per row: (1/N)*rstd * ( N*dy_hat - sum(dy_hat) - xhat*sum(dy_hat*xhat) )
abi: - schema_id == 0 => default eps (1e-5 in launcher usage)
- if schema mismatch or payload too short => default eps
expected_attr_schema_id for fwd variants is set to 'LNEP' (note: launcher also accepts schema_id==0).
notes: Row-major contiguous is enforced strictly via stride[1]==1 and stride[0]==shape[1].
Threads per row are chosen as a power-of-two up to 256 based on N (pick_threads_pow2_le_256).
Forward uses block reductions (warp shuffles + shared memory) to compute sum and sumsq per row.
Mean/Rstd are written by thread0 of each row block.
Backward dX is computed per row; dGamma/dBeta is computed per column (one block per c, threads over M).
For very large M,N, the dGamma/dBeta kernel (grid=N blocks) can be heavy; consider 2D tiling or two-stage reduction later.

variants.name: layernorm_fwd_f32_contig2d
supported: X,Y: dtype=f32, rank=2, contiguous row-major (stride[1]==1, stride[0]==N)
If affine (ni==3): Gamma,Beta are f32 1D contiguous len=N
variants.notes: Kernel: layernorm_fwd_f32_kernel. Launch: grid=(M,1,1), block=(threads,1,1) where threads=pow2<=256 based on N.

variants.name: layernorm_fwd_f16_contig2d
supported: X,Y: dtype=f16, rank=2, contiguous row-major (stride[1]==1, stride[0]==N)
If affine (ni==3): Gamma,Beta are f16 1D contiguous len=N
variants.notes: Kernel: layernorm_fwd_f16_kernel. Internals accumulate in f32; store Y in f16.

variants.name: layernorm_bwd_f32_contig2d
supported: X,dY,dX: dtype=f32, rank=2, contiguous row-major; shapes match X[M,N]
If affine: Gamma is f32 1D contiguous len=N; dGamma,dBeta are f32 1D contiguous len=N
notes: Pass A: layernorm_bwd_dx_f32_kernel, grid=(M), block=pow2<=256 based on N
Pass B (affine only): layernorm_bwd_dg_db_f32_kernel, grid=(N), block=pow2<=256 based on M

variants.name: layernorm_bwd_f16_contig2d
supported: X,dY,dX: dtype=f16, rank=2, contiguous row-major; shapes match X[M,N]
If affine: Gamma is f16 1D contiguous len=N; dGamma,dBeta are f32 1D contiguous len=N
notes: Pass A: layernorm_bwd_dx_f16_kernel, grid=(M), block=pow2<=256 based on N
Pass B (affine only): layernorm_bwd_dg_db_f16_kernel, grid=(N), block=pow2<=256 based on M

suites.name: forward_basic
suites.desc: Forward correctness: affine/noaff, eps handling, f16 vs f32.

suites.name: backward_basic
suites.desc: Backward correctness: noaff vs affine gradients, f16 vs f32.

suites.name: supported_gating
suites.desc: Reject non-2D, non-contig, wrong strides, or mismatched lengths.

experiments.title: Vectorize forward loads/stores (half2/float2)
experiments.change: Add vectorized path when N is even and pointers aligned, using half2 for f16 and float2 for f32.
experiments.why: Current kernels are scalar per element; vectorization can reduce instruction count and improve memory throughput.
experiments.hypothesis: Lower latency for large N; higher achieved bandwidth.
experiments.proof: ncu: gld/gst efficiency, dram throughput; correctness vs reference.
experiments.next: Also vectorize reduction with pairwise sums to reduce rounding error.

experiments.title: Two-stage reduction for dGamma/dBeta
experiments.change: Replace per-column single-block reduction over M with a two-stage reduction (partial sums per block then finalize).
experiments.why: Current dg/db kernel uses one block per column; for large M this becomes slow and may exceed efficient thread utilization.
experiments.hypothesis: Better scaling when M is large (e.g., batch*seq).
experiments.proof: Benchmark large M (e.g., 8192) and compare runtime; verify numerics.
experiments.next: Fuse dx and dg/db passes if beneficial (tradeoff: more registers/shared).

experiments.title: Welford variance for improved numerical stability
experiments.change: Compute mean/var using Welford online algorithm instead of sum/sumsq.
experiments.why: sum/sumsq can accumulate error for large N and large magnitude values.
experiments.hypothesis: Closer match to PyTorch reference and fewer negative var clamp events.
experiments.proof: Compare max error vs reference across random distributions with large N; check how often var<0 clamp triggers.
experiments.next: Optionally keep sum/sumsq for speed and add a 'stable' flag.

measurements.notes: Report latency and effective bandwidth (read X (+G/B) and write Y plus mean/rstd). TFLOP/s not primary.
